title: Strategy Identity Drift: Bot Is Entering Momentum Trades, Not Mean Reversion
analysis: Two of the three SUBMITTED trades in this journal are structurally momentum entries, not mean reversion: NVDA on 2026-05-15 fired 'RSI>65 (strong momentum)', 'AboveMA20>1%', 'ADX>25 (trending)' — every signal is the opposite of the mean reversion thesis. AAPL on 2026-05-18 fired identical anti-MR signals: 'RSI>65', 'AboveMA20>1%', 'ADX>25 (trending)'. The signal scoring system in CLAUDE.md only defines mean reversion entry signals (RSI<35, RSI<45, BelowBB, BelowMA20), yet the bot is generating and acting on signals labelled 'RSI>65 (strong momentum)' and 'AboveMA20>1%' — signals that do not exist in the documented ruleset. This is not parameter drift; the bot has developed an undocumented parallel signal pathway that fires on the opposite conditions and bypasses the ADX>30 trend filter (NVDA entry had ADX>25, not >30, so the hard filter technically didn't block it, but the spirit of Rule 6 was violated). The MSFT SELL on 2026-05-18 with only signal_score=1 ('ADX<25') and stop_loss=0 also indicates the exit logic is partially disconnected from documented rules.
rationale: A mean reversion system that silently enters momentum trades has undefined risk characteristics. Mean reversion and momentum have opposite loss profiles: MR losses are typically small and frequent; momentum losses can be large and sudden. Mixing both without explicit rules means position sizing, stop placement, and profit targets are calibrated for the wrong trade type. The NVDA momentum entry used a 0.5x ATR stop designed for MR — catastrophically tight for a trending instrument. This needs to be either explicitly permitted with separate rules, or hard-blocked.

insight.why_now: Two of three live trades in the observation window are momentum entries. This is not an edge case — it represents 67% of actual capital deployment. The pattern will compound as the bot 'learns' these trades are not rejected.
insight.purpose: Force the system to either (a) explicitly define and separately govern a momentum/breakout overlay with its own sizing, stops, and filters, or (b) hard-block any entry where RSI>50 or price is AboveMA20, closing the undocumented signal pathway entirely.
insight.expected_effect: Eliminates strategy identity confusion, ensures position sizing and stop logic match the actual trade type being taken, and prevents the bot from taking maximum-risk trades (trending momentum) with minimum-size stops (0.5x ATR MR stops).
insight.risks: If momentum trades have been profitable, blocking them reduces opportunity. The correct response is to govern them explicitly, not eliminate them blindly. Requires audit of NVDA and AAPL trade outcomes before deciding.

current_rule: 6. TREND FILTER: If ADX > 30, regime is TRENDING — do NOT take mean reversion signals.
proposed_rule: 6. TREND FILTER: If ADX > 25 OR RSI > 55 OR price is AboveMA20, the mean reversion condition is NOT met — do NOT take a mean reversion entry. Any signal firing 'RSI>65', 'AboveMA20>1%', or 'ADX>25 (trending)' as a BUY justification is a MOMENTUM signal, not a mean reversion signal, and must be REJECTED unless a separate MOMENTUM_MODE is explicitly enabled in config. Default: MOMENTUM_MODE = false.

title: Concentrated Watchlist in Two Correlated Tech Names Is Starving Trade Flow
analysis: Of the 50 journal entries, 38 are pure SKIPs with signal_score=0. Of the 9 non-trivial entries (score>0 or SUBMITTED), 7 involve META or MSFT — both large-cap tech, highly correlated (typical 60-day correlation ~0.75-0.85). The bot held both simultaneously for the entire observation window (open_positions=2 on nearly every entry). Sector data shows Technology down -0.73% over 5 days while Energy is up +4.96% and Financials +0.32%. The bot has zero exposure to the two outperforming sectors and is structurally unable to find mean reversion setups because its entire watchlist appears to be tech names that are either already held or in a mild directional drift. The VIX at 18.48 ('elevated') is a marginal environment for mean reversion — workable, but requires a wider, more diversified symbol universe to find setups where RSI<35 and BelowBB conditions are actually met. The repeated REJECTED signals on META and MSFT (6 rejections across May 13-14) show the bot is generating signals on instruments it cannot trade, wasting cycles and masking the real problem: the watchlist is too narrow and sector-concentrated.
rationale: Mean reversion requires instruments that oscillate. A two-stock tech watchlist in an environment where tech is drifting down -0.73% (mild trend, not oscillation) produces either no signals or signals on already-held positions. Expanding to include ETFs (XLE for Energy, XLF for Financials, GLD, IWM) and defensive names (XLV, XLP constituents) would diversify regime exposure and surface valid MR setups in sectors currently showing range-bound behaviour. Correlation-adjusted sizing would also become meaningful — currently two correlated tech positions represent effectively 3% portfolio heat from a single factor bet.

insight.why_now: 38/50 entries (76%) are zero-signal SKIPs. The bot is not finding trades because the watchlist does not contain instruments with active MR setups in the current environment. Energy (+4.96% 5d) has likely already broken out, but sector ETF mean reversion around that move's retracement is a valid opportunity being missed entirely.
insight.purpose: Diversify the tradeable universe to include at least 2-3 sector ETFs (XLE, XLF, GLD, IWM) and reduce single-sector concentration. ETFs have natural mean reversion properties due to diversification and are ideal for the strategy.
insight.expected_effect: Increase valid signal frequency from the current ~4% hit rate (2 clean MR signals in 50 entries) to a structurally higher baseline. Reduce correlation between simultaneously held positions.
insight.risks: Wider universe increases monitoring complexity. ETF moves are smaller in absolute terms, making commissions relatively more significant at VIX<20. Must verify R:R ≥ 1.5 is achievable on lower-volatility ETFs before adding them.

current_rule: - Universe: US Stocks/ETFs via Alpaca + Crypto via Binance/CCXT
proposed_rule:
- Universe: US Stocks/ETFs via Alpaca + Crypto via Binance/CCXT
- WATCHLIST DIVERSITY RULE: At all times, the active watchlist must include at least 3 distinct GICS sectors. No more than 2 watchlist symbols may be from the same sector (e.g., max 2 tech names). Mandatory ETF coverage: at least one of [SPY, QQQ, IWM, GLD, XLE, XLF, XLV] must be on the active scan list. Rationale: ETFs have structural mean reversion properties; sector diversity ensures valid setups exist across regime rotations.

title: Locked Capital in Two Stale Positions Is Blocking New Entries for 4+ Days
analysis: The bot held exactly 2 open positions (META and MSFT) from the first entry on 2026-05-12 through at least 2026-05-17 — a minimum of 5 calendar days (3+ trading days). The TIME STOP rule states 'Exit any position open longer than 3 days regardless of P&L,' yet both positions persisted beyond this threshold without any SELL entries appearing until the MSFT SELL on 2026-05-18. During this entire window, the bot repeatedly generated valid signals on META (score=3, R:R=3.7 on 2026-05-13) and MSFT (score=3, R:R=2.58-2.70 on 2026-05-13; score=2 on 2026-05-14) but rejected all of them because it 'already holds' the names. The time stop appears non-functional or overridden. Meanwhile, account value oscillated between $98,229 and $98,543 — essentially flat — while the bot watched valid setups on its own holdings expire. The daily P&L on 2026-05-18 at decision time was -$306 to -$355, suggesting the stale positions were actively losing. The MSFT exit on 2026-05-18 at entry_price=419.81 with stop_loss=0 is also anomalous — a SELL with no stop loss field and score=1 suggests a time-stop or manual exit, not a signal-driven exit, and the missing stop on a SELL order indicates the exit logic has a data integrity issue.
rationale: The 3-day time stop exists precisely to prevent capital from being locked in range-bound positions that have failed to revert. When the time stop is not executing, the bot's effective max positions drops from 5 to (5 minus stale holds), and the no-add-to-existing-position rule compounds this by preventing re-entry even when the setup re-qualifies. The combination creates a capital lockup pattern where the bot is fully committed to underperforming positions while watching valid setups expire. The zero stop_loss on the MSFT SELL also suggests the exit pipeline has a validation gap that needs closing.

insight.why_now: The 5-day observation window shows the bot was effectively paralyzed — 2 stale positions blocking 3 available slots, 6 valid signals rejected on the held names, and the time stop rule not firing. This is the single most mechanical fix available.
insight.purpose: Enforce the time stop rule programmatically and add a sell-order validation requirement (stop_loss must not be 0 or null on any SELL order that is not a hard stop execution). Also add an explicit rule that a position triggering a new entry signal on the same symbol after day 2 should accelerate the time stop review.
insight.expected_effect: Frees capital on day 3, allows the bot to re-enter at the new (better) setup price it was already identifying, and eliminates the pattern of holding losers while watching valid re-entries expire. On the observed data, this would have unlocked META and MSFT for re-entry on 2026-05-13 at R:R of 2.58-3.70.
insight.risks: Exiting on day 3 at a loss and immediately re-entering the same symbol at a lower price could be perceived as churning. Must ensure re-entry requires the full signal threshold (score ≥ 2) and is not triggered by the same marginal setup that prompted the original exit.

current_rule: - Time stop: Exit any position open longer than 3 days regardless of P&L
proposed_rule: - Time stop: Exit any position open longer than 3 trading days regardless of P&L. This rule is MANDATORY and cannot be overridden by open P&L, missing signals, or any other condition. On day 3 close (14:45 EST), if position is still open, generate a SELL order automatically. SELL orders must always include a valid stop_loss value (not 0, not null) — use current bid minus 0.1x ATR as the execution floor. After a time-stop exit, the symbol re-enters the scan universe immediately and may be re-entered if signal_score ≥ 2 and R:R ≥ 1.5 are met on the next cycle.
